title: Minimum Rounds for Feistel Indifferentiability
summary: Five rounds are insufficient and ten rounds suffice, but the minimum number of rounds required for indifferentiability remains unresolved, including whether fewer than ten suffice.

formal_statement.body: For a Feistel network whose round functions are independent and random, 5 rounds are insufficient for indifferentiability from a random permutation, while 14 rounds are sufficient. The unresolved task is to determine the minimum number of rounds $r$ that suffices for this indifferentiability, in particular whether fewer than 10 rounds suffice, given that a 10-round network is known to suffice.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography studying indifferentiability of Feistel networks from random permutations.
assumptions: The round functions are independent and random.
parameters: The round count $r$, whose minimum sufficient value for indifferentiability is sought
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the minimum number of rounds sufficient for indifferentiability, in particular whether fewer than 10 rounds suffice.

citations.label: 10-Round Feistel is Indifferentiable from an Ideal Cipher

progress.summary: The source presents the issue as an efficiency question, with prior work showing that 5 rounds are insufficient and 14 are sufficient. This work establishes sufficiency for 10 rounds but leaves the optimal round count unresolved.
citation_labels: Dana Dachman-Soled et al., 10-Round Feistel is Indifferentiable from an Ideal Cipher
